title: Gut Article, Phases 4 and 5 (Batch 14)
intro: Phase 4's organ check and Phase 5's opener and steps read AI when Pangram checked their sections by themselves. Each card has the fixed version, and the whole protocol section reads [Human Written, 0% AI](https://www.pangram.com/history/3ff02029-f214-43d0-a5f9-84ba75f13c07) with them in, all High or Medium.
These replace both tries of Phase 5's first two steps (drafts C and D), so draft D's reading isn't needed anymore.

suggestions.title: Phase 4: the organ check joins the paragraph that gives its reason, and the bile case says what it is

edits.before: Benjamin Brown (Digestive Health Solution) is the only source for this phase. If even the "Nuclear Option" failed, you can cross the microbiome off the list. The problem is likely an organ that isn't working right, or environmental toxicity or your brain's false danger signals (those two are Phase 6, below).
edits.after: Benjamin Brown (Digestive Health Solution) is the only source for this phase. If even the "Nuclear Option" failed, you can cross the microbiome off the list. The problem is likely an organ that isn't working right, or environmental toxicity or your brain's false danger signals (those two are Phase 6, below). So check your organs, starting with your pancreas: if it doesn't make enough digestive enzymes, called Exocrine Pancreatic Insufficiency, you'd test for that with Stool Elastase, and treat it with high-dose enzymes. Or is it your bile? If too much of it reaches your colon, you get diarrhea, called Bile Acid Diarrhea. Get a SeHCAT test for it, and if it comes back positive, take bile binders.

suggestions.reads_label: Phase 4's first paragraph as it would read
suggestions.what: The one numbered step joins the paragraph above it, and the bile case asks the reader first
suggestions.why: The step read AI in the cut of Phases 3 to 6 and Low in the cut of Phases 4 and 5, and its Bile Acid Diarrhea case read Low in the whole article (draft C). By itself the step read AI in every wording I tried, because alone it has no reason in it: its "So" points to the paragraph above ("The problem is likely an organ ..."). So the step joins that paragraph, without its number, and without "(Brown)", since the paragraph already names Brown as the phase's only source. The bile case was the last part that read AI, when it copied the pancreas case's pattern word for word. It now asks the reader first, the way Phase 6 asks about mold, and says what Bile Acid Diarrhea is: too much bile reaching your colon gives you diarrhea ([NICE DG44](https://nice.org.uk/guidance/dg44/documents/topic-description): bile acids that aren't absorbed reach the colon, and the excess there causes diarrhoea).
suggestions.stays: Both organs, both tests (Stool Elastase, SeHCAT) and both treatments (high-dose enzymes, bile binders); the paragraph's first three sentences, word for word.

suggestions.title: Phase 5, step 1: the yogurt, with you and Davis doing things

edits.before: Start by re-seeding with Davis's high-dose "SIBO Yogurt", fermented for 36 hours. It contains L. reuteri, to heal the lining and boost oxytocin, and L. gasseri, to produce bacteriocins that kill SIBO.
edits.after: Start by re-seeding your gut with Davis's high-dose "SIBO Yogurt", which you ferment at home for 36 hours. He picked its bacteria for what they do: L. reuteri heals your gut lining and boosts oxytocin (the "love hormone"), and L. gasseri makes bacteriocins, natural antibiotics that kill SIBO.

suggestions.what: You ferment the yogurt, Davis picked its bacteria, and oxytocin and bacteriocins are explained
suggestions.why: The step read Low in your whole article (draft B) and AI, Medium in both cuts. The yogurt and its bacteria were the subjects, with "to heal ..." and "to produce ..." clauses. Now you ferment it and Davis picked its bacteria for what they do, each bacterium does its job, and the two terms a reader wouldn't know get a plain gloss where they come up: oxytocin (the "love hormone"), bacteriocins (natural antibiotics). Davis says he chose the strains of his original SIBO yogurt himself, and that they make bacteriocins that kill SIBO's species ([Defiant Health Radio](https://www.buzzsprout.com/1795054/episodes/17783323-here-s-a-microbe-you-should-know-about-bacillus-subtilis)).

suggestions.title: Phase 5, step 2: feeding the bacteria with plants, slowly

edits.before: Then feed the new healthy bacteria. Bulsiewicz says to slowly titrate plant diversity back into your diet, aiming for 30+ different plants per week. Does anyone count their plants?
edits.after: Then feed the new healthy bacteria with plants, slowly, the way Bulsiewicz says: add a few new kinds at a time, until you eat 30+ different plants a week. Does anyone count their plants?

reads.text: Then feed the new healthy bacteria with plants, slowly, the way Bulsiewicz says: add a few new kinds at a time, until you eat 30+ different plants a week. Does anyone count their plants?

suggestions.what: One sentence that says how: "with plants, slowly, the way Bulsiewicz says: add a few new kinds at a time"
suggestions.why: The step read Low in your whole article (draft B) and AI, High in both cuts. The short "Then feed the new healthy bacteria." now carries its how in the same sentence, and "add a few new kinds at a time" says what "slowly titrate plant diversity back" meant. Bulsiewicz's reason for going slowly: more fiber at once can bring gas and bloating while your gut bacteria adapt ([Plant Based News](https://plantbasednews.org/lifestyle/health/gut-doctor-survival-guide-bloating-plant-based-diet/)). Your "Does anyone count their plants?" stays right after the number it jokes about.
suggestions.stays: The 30+ plants a week, Bulsiewicz, and your "Does anyone count their plants?"
